person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: We present a residual learning framework to ease the training of networks that are substantially deeper than those used previously.

span.label: the degradation problem in very deep neural networks
span.quote: When deeper networks are able to start converging, a degradation problem has been exposed: with the network depth increasing, accuracy gets saturated (which might be unsurprising) and then degrades rapidly.

span.label: computational-experiment
span.quote: We present comprehensive experiments on ImageNet [36] to show the degradation problem and evaluate our method.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: reformulate each layer to learn a residual function via identity shortcut connections, so very deep networks are easier to optimize and avoid the depth-degradation problem
span.quote: these residual networks are easier to optimize, and can gain accuracy from considerably increased depth

span.label: why residual mappings are easier to optimize remains an open question
span.note: what this limits: the explanation of why residual learning works: THIS HYPOTHESIS, HOWEVER, IS STILL AN OPEN QUESTION
span.quote: This hypothesis, however, is still an open question.

span.label: The cause of the optimisation difficulty in deep plain nets is not explained.
span.note: what this limits: the account of what goes wrong in plain deep nets: THE REASON FOR SUCH OPTIMIZATION DIFFICULTIES WILL BE STUDIED IN THE FUTURE
span.quote: The reason for such optimization difficulties will be studied in the future.

span.label: Extremely deep (1202-layer) models remain problematic.
span.note: what this limits: the very deep regime: THERE ARE STILL OPEN PROBLEMS ON SUCH AGGRESSIVELY DEEP MODELS
span.quote: But there are still open problems on such aggressively deep models.

span.label: The 1202-layer net's worse test error is attributed to overfitting from excess capacity on a small dataset.
span.note: what this limits: the 1202-layer result specifically: THE 1202-LAYER NETWORK MAY BE UNNECESSARILY LARGE (19.4M) FOR THIS SMALL DATASET
span.quote: The 1202-layer network may be unnecessarily large (19.4M) for this small dataset.

span.label: The premise that multiple nonlinear layers can asymptotically approximate complicated functions is unproven.
span.note: what this limits: the approximation premise rather than the optimisation question of item 0: THE PREMISE THAT MULTIPLE NONLINEAR LAYERS CAN ASYMPTOTICALLY APPROXIMATE COMPLICATED FUNCTIONS is stated as a hypothesis that is STILL AN OPEN QUESTION
span.quote: This hypothesis, however, is still an open question.

span.label: Stronger regularisation was not explored and might improve the CIFAR-10 results.
span.note: what this limits: the CIFAR-10 results: COMBINING WITH STRONGER REGULARIZATION MAY IMPROVE RESULTS, WHICH WE WILL STUDY IN THE FUTURE
span.quote: But combining with stronger regularization may improve results, which we will study in the future.

span.label: The scenario that motivates the design is conceded to be unlikely in practice.
span.note: what this limits: the intuition given for residual learning: the authors concede that in real cases it is unlikely that identity mappings are optimal
span.quote: In real cases, it is unlikely that identity mappings are optimal

span.label: The paper's central premise is labelled a hypothesis by its authors.
span.note: what this limits: the claim that residual mappings are easier to optimize: the authors present it as a hypothesis rather than as a demonstrated result
span.quote: We hypothesize that it is easier to optimize the residual mapping than to optimize the original, unreferenced mapping

span.label: overfitting as the cause of the degradation problem
span.quote: Unexpectedly, such degradation is not caused by overfitting, and adding more layers to a suitably deep model leads to higher training error, as reported in [11, 42] and thoroughly verified by our experiments

span.label: vanishing gradients as the cause of the optimisation difficulty in plain nets
span.quote: We argue that this optimization difficulty is unlikely to be caused by vanishing gradients. These plain networks are trained with BN [16], which ensures forward propagated signals to have non-zero variances. We also verify that the backward propagated gradients exhibit healthy norms with BN. So neither forward nor backward signals vanish

span.quote: Unexpectedly, such degradation is not caused by overfitting, and adding more layers to a suitably deep model leads to higher training error, as reported in [11, 42] and thoroughly verified by our experiments

span.label: overfitting

span.quote: We argue that this optimization difficulty is unlikely to be caused by vanishing gradients. These plain networks are trained with BN [16], which ensures forward propagated signals to have non-zero variances. We also verify that the backward propagated gradients exhibit healthy norms with BN. So neither forward nor backward signals vanish

span.label: optimization difficulty
span.quote: We argue that this optimization difficulty is unlikely to be caused by vanishing gradients

span.label: residual mapping
span.quote: We hypothesize that it is easier to optimize the residual mapping than to optimize the original, unreferenced mapping

span.label: identity mapping
span.quote: In real cases, it is unlikely that identity mappings are optimal

span.label: the degradation problem - IDENTIFIED BY TRAINING ERROR, NOT TEST ERROR: accuracy saturates then degrades rapidly with depth, and the authors' point is that this is NOT overfitting because adding layers raises the TRAINING error - the distinction is what makes it an optimisation problem rather than a generalisation one
span.quote: Unexpectedly, such degradation is not caused by overfitting, and adding more layers to a suitably deep model leads to higher training error, as reported in [11, 42] and thoroughly verified by our experiments

span.label: an identity mapping - AN IDEALISATION THE PAPER WITHDRAWS: the argument for residual learning runs through the case where identity mappings are optimal and the solver can drive the weights to zero, and the authors then state in their own words that in real cases this is unlikely
span.quote: In real cases, it is unlikely that identity mappings are optimal

span.label: the residual mapping - A REFORMULATION, PRESENTED AS A HYPOTHESIS: instead of fitting the desired underlying mapping the layers fit its residual, and the claim that this is easier to optimise is given in the authors' own words as something they hypothesize
span.quote: We hypothesize that it is easier to optimize the residual mapping than to optimize the original, unreferenced mapping

span.label: extends → plain deep convolutional networks (the degradation problem)
span.quote: with the network depth increasing, accuracy gets saturated

span.label: replicates → prior reports [11, 42] that adding layers to a deep model raises training error
span.quote: Unexpectedly, such degradation is not caused by overfitting, and adding more layers to a suitably deep model leads to higher training error, as reported in [11, 42] and thoroughly verified by our experiments.

span.label: builds-on → VGG nets [41]
span.quote: Our plain baselines (Fig. 3, middle) are mainly inspired by the philosophy of VGG nets [41] (Fig. 3, left).

span.label: builds-on → Faster R-CNN [32]
span.quote: We adopt Faster R-CNN [32] as the detection method.

span.label: extends → highway networks [42, 43]
span.quote: These gates are data-dependent and have parameters, in contrast to our identity shortcuts that are parameter-free.

span.label: RETRACTED (CONTRADICTED BY ITS OWN SPAN) · overfitting —causes→ degradation
span.note: RETRACTED: CONTRADICTED BY ITS OWN SPAN.
